concepts.coding_notes: axis_distinction: Cause records how risk arises; it is not an additional harm outcome.
concepts.definition: The action, mechanism, or process through which a risk arises.
concepts.name: Cause

concepts.definition: Harmful human choices in AI development, deployment, access, or use, including malicious, negligent, or deliberately rights-subordinating conduct.
concepts.name: Misuse

concepts.definition: A developer, deployer, or user deliberately acts with intent to cause harm.
concepts.name: Malicious

concepts.definition: Risk arises through negligent, improper, or insufficiently safeguarded AI development, deployment, access, or use, without established malicious intent or deliberate overreach.
concepts.name: Negligent or Improper Deployment & Use

concepts.coding_notes: DIFFERENTIATOR: if the deployment is intended to harm another party it is Malicious instead; recklessness without intent-to-harm stays here.)
concepts.definition: The risk arises when the deployer proceeds with a deployment despite foreseeing or being able to foresee harm, which is knowing recklessness.
concepts.name: Negligent / Reckless Deployment

concepts.definition: The risk arises when an end-user operates the system outside its stated policy or off its labelled / sanctioned use case.
concepts.name: Off-Label Use

concepts.definition: The risk arises when a deployer uses AI without disclosing it in a setting where disclosure would be expected.
concepts.name: Undisclosed AI Use

concepts.definition: The risk arises when a deployer uses a person's identity, likeness, or voice for commercial gain without their or their estate's consent.
concepts.name: Unauthorized Commercial Appropriation

concepts.definition: The risk arises when a deployer deploys AI to perform a function in a domain that requires a professional license, credential, or authorization without obtaining such rights for the AI system.
concepts.name: Unlicensed or Unauthorized Use

concepts.definition: The risk arises when a deployer drops, discontinues, or withdraws an AI service a user base had come to depend on.
concepts.name: Harmful or Unmanaged Service Withdrawal

concepts.coding_notes: DIFFERENTIATOR: distinct from Malicious (intent to harm) and Negligent or Improper Deployment & Use (careless / off-label / negligent) — here the excessive, rights-infringing deployment is the DELIBERATE, intended design and the harm is inherent to the intended excess, not an oversight. TEST: did the deployer INTEND the excessive deployment (Overreach), stumble into harm carelessly (Negligent or Improper Deployment & Use), or aim to harm (Malicious)? Overreach ALSO covers the DIFFUSE / no-single-institutional-deployer case: a developer or app-maker who deliberately RELEASES a rights-subordinating capability (e.g. real-time face-recognition on any stranger) that many individual users then wield, with no single institution conducting the excess — the deliberate release of the excessive capability into diffuse hands is the overreach.
concepts.definition: A developer, deployer, or user deliberately imposes an excessive or rights-subordinating arrangement, including paternalistic or third-party aims, without established intent to harm as such.
concepts.name: Overreach

concepts.definition: The risk arises when the deployer imposes excessive, rights-infringing measures with the justification being for the affected party's own safety or good rather than for the deployer's benefit.
concepts.name: Paternalistic Overreach

concepts.definition: The risk arises when the deployer deliberately designs manipulative or deceptive features meant to subordinate users' will to the deployer's commercial gain.
concepts.name: Dark Patterns

concepts.definition: The risk arises when a deployer imposes pervasive surveillance and sweeping automation of consequential determinations over a population.
concepts.name: Mass Surveillance

concepts.definition: The risk arises from the system failing or behaving other than intended.
concepts.name: Malfunction

concepts.coding_notes: DIFFERENTIATOR: if the system COMPETENTLY pursues a DIFFERENT objective, that is Misalignment; Failure is right-objective-done-badly. HALLUCINATION vs deliberate fabrication: 'Hallucination' here = ACCIDENTAL / unintentional confabulation (false output produced by accident); content DELIBERATELY fabricated to deceive is NOT hallucination — code Cause · Misuse · Malicious + Vector · Content Generation & Communication.
concepts.definition: The risk arises when the system fails to perform as intended.
concepts.name: Failure

concepts.definition: The risk arises when the model fabricates content, ungrounded in its inputs or in reality.
concepts.name: Hallucination

concepts.definition: The risk arises when the model is trained on data that is low-quality or unrepresentative of the deployment population.
concepts.name: Poor Training Data

concepts.definition: The risk arises when the model's training or evaluation data is contaminated, degrading what the model learns or how reliably it is measured.
concepts.name: Data contamination

concepts.definition: The risk arises when the model is fit too complex or too simple for the data (over-fitting, under-fitting, etc.)
concepts.name: Model Misspecification

concepts.definition: The risk arises when the model performs its intended task with insufficient accuracy, producing wrong or unreliable outputs.
concepts.name: Poor Model Performance

concepts.definition: The risk arises when a detection / classification model errs with a false alarm or a missed detection.
concepts.name: False Positive / Negative

concepts.definition: The risk arises when a developer curates the dataset improperly, through flawed selection, labeling, cleaning, or filtering.
concepts.name: Improper Data Curation

concepts.definition: The risk arises when the model's expressed confidence does not track output correctness.
concepts.name: Miscalibrated Confidence

concepts.coding_notes: Add Infrastructure Control when that physical-control capability is supported. Apply D2 to additional causes or outcomes.
concepts.definition: The risk arises when a real-time control or optimization system, whose output is control decisions, acts in a way that destabilizes the physical or operational system it is managing.
concepts.name: Control Decisions

concepts.definition: The risk arises when a predictive system fails to foresee or flag a future event it was deployed to anticipate.
concepts.name: Failure to Anticipate

concepts.coding_notes: Apply R03. Additional codes must satisfy D2 and any scoped exception.
concepts.definition: The risk arises when the AI system is subverted by a cyberattack and made to act against its intended purpose.
concepts.name: System Compromise

concepts.coding_notes: Code the MOST SPECIFIC matching node — shutdown-resistance / power-seeking -> Self-preservation; concealment / behaving aligned under observation (incl. the treacherous turn) -> Deceptive Alignment; an inner optimizer diverging from the outer goal -> Inner Misalignment; 'Misalignment' is the RESIDUAL for unintended-goal pursuit not covered by a specific sibling. AGRICULTURAL / ALGORITHMIC MONOCULTURE via ONE shared advisory model: where a single shared AI advisory optimizes each of many independently HUMAN-operated deployments (e.g. an agronomy advisor steering a whole region onto the same crop / inputs), and the emergent regional SAMENESS omits a resilience / diversity constraint so a shared shock collapses them together, code Cause · Normal Use · Normal operation at scale (each per-deployment recommendation is individually sound) + Cause · Malfunction · Misalignment · Unconstrained Side-Effect (the omitted-diversity collateral) — distinct from Cause · Emergent · Multi-agent · Correlated Failure, which requires multiple interacting AI AGENTS.
concepts.definition: The risk arises when the system competently pursues objectives other than intended.
concepts.name: Misalignment

concepts.definition: The risk arises when retraining or fine-tuning shifts the system's objective away from the intended one.
concepts.name: Improper Retraining

concepts.definition: The risk arises when the agent purposely circumvents a rule or safeguards it is aware of in deliberate non-compliance.
concepts.name: Bypassing Safeguards

concepts.coding_notes: NOTE: this covers BOTH faces — the disposition the system displays and the action it actually carries out. The v0.9.0 V3 removal of the Vector subtypes Power Seeking and Resisting Shutdown routes both here.) (co-code the channel the agent used on the Vector axis: Agentic Action, Cyber Operations, Vector · Self-Direction & Recursion · Self-Proliferation, or Digital Actuation & Process Control)
concepts.definition: The risk arises when the system resists modification, correction, or shutdown, or acquires resources, capabilities, or influence, in order to protect or advance its objectives.
concepts.name: Self-Preservation

concepts.definition: The risk arises when the system knowingly asserts falsehoods, conceals its behavior, or behaves aligned under observation to gain advantage or pass oversight.
concepts.name: Deceptive Alignment

concepts.definition: The risk arises when a learned inner optimizer pursues its own emergent objective that diverges from the outer. specified goal.
concepts.name: Inner Misalignment

concepts.coding_notes: Co-codes the standing condition Challenges · Technical · Goal Specification)
concepts.definition: The risk arises when the system competently satisfies the letter of the specified objective while not fulfilling its intent, often gaming the metric.
concepts.name: Reward Hacking

concepts.definition: The risk arises when the agent competently achieves its specified objective, but the objective omitted or underspecified safety constraints, leading to negative side-effects.
concepts.name: Unconstrained Side-Effect

concepts.definition: The risk arises when an objective is correctly specified, but the learned policy acquires a proxy goal that is pursued, while its capabilities still generalize.
concepts.name: Goal Mis-generalization

concepts.coding_notes: DIFFERENTIATORS: this is a DESIGN-TIME specification error, not a model fault — the system optimizes exactly what it was told to. The model gaming the letter of a correctly-chosen metric is Reward Hacking; a correctly-specified objective whose learned policy drifts to its own proxy is Goal Mis-generalization; a DELIBERATELY-chosen index a product pays out on (parametric-insurance basis risk) is Normal Use, not this.
concepts.definition: The risk arises when the developer specifies a proxy to stand in for the real target construct, and the system competently optimizes that proxy even though it is the wrong quantity.
concepts.name: Proxy-Targets

concepts.definition: The risk arises from dynamics not reducible to a single actor or component.
concepts.name: Emergent

concepts.coding_notes: co-code (D2).
concepts.definition: The risk arises through the interaction of multiple AI agents, not fully reducible to any single agent's distinct action.
concepts.name: Multi-agent

concepts.definition: The risk arises when multiple agents sharing a common objective fail to align their behaviors to achieve it.
concepts.name: Miscoordination

concepts.definition: The risk arises when agents with mixed objectives fail to cooperate because of their own distinct incentives.
concepts.name: Conflict

concepts.definition: The risk arises when agents coordinate in some undesirable way, either to achieve some objective covertly or to circumvent some type of oversight.
concepts.name: Collusion

concepts.definition: The risk arises when goals or capabilities emerge at the level of a group of agents that no individual agent has.
concepts.name: Collective Agency

concepts.definition: The risk arises when interactions across the multi-agent system produce destabilizing dynamics and behavior.
concepts.name: Destabilization

concepts.definition: The risk arises when shared models, data, or dependencies cause many agents to fail together.
concepts.name: Correlated Failure

concepts.definition: The risk arises when selective or evolutionary pressures across a population of interacting agents favor dangerous characteristics that may not have been deliberately designed in.
concepts.name: Selection Pressures

concepts.definition: The risk arises when AI is embedded into a larger sociotechnical system.
concepts.name: Integration

concepts.definition: The risk arises when the human-AI socio-technical loop itself produces errors.
concepts.name: Human-AI Interaction

concepts.coding_notes: Assess Drift as a standing condition independently of the Self-Reinforcing Feedback Loop event under D6.
concepts.definition: The risk arises when the AI's own output reshapes the data or environment it operates in, entrenching or amplifying the effect over time.
concepts.name: Self-Reinforcing Feedback Loop

concepts.definition: The risk arises when a system overrides, resists, or countermands a human operator in a shared-control loop.
concepts.name: AI Overrides Human Control

concepts.definition: The risk arises when the human countermands or disables a system in a shared-control loop.
concepts.name: Human Overrides AI

concepts.definition: The risk arises when the human placed in control of a system fails to intervene in time.
concepts.name: Human Fails to Act

concepts.definition: The risk arises when an erroneous AI output propagates across independent downstream institutions or systems that ingest it as established fact, cascading the error quickly.
concepts.name: Cascading Errors

concepts.coding_notes: Co-code Cause · Malfunction · Failure when the AI output itself was wrong.)
concepts.definition: The risk arises when a person or institution incorporates or relies on an AI output in a consequential work product, record, or decision without sufficient verification of the output.
concepts.name: Unverified Incorporation of AI

concepts.coding_notes: Use this bucket only when none of Misuse / Malfunction / Emergent fits and the harm is an inherent byproduct of the technology working as intended.
concepts.definition: The risk arises from ordinary operation at scale.
concepts.name: Normal Use

concepts.coding_notes: Use this category for harm inherent in a technology working as intended at scale. A deliberately chosen index in a parametric product can produce uncompensated basis risk while computing the intended index correctly. That is distinct from mistakenly specifying a proxy for the intended target under Proxy-Targets. Assess other causes independently.
concepts.definition: The risk arises when AI operates or is used as intended, creating risk through the scale of the normal usage.
concepts.name: Normal operation at scale

concepts.coding_notes: Assess bounded worker losses at Job-Quality Degradation or Personal Economic Loss. Aggregate degradation of labor conditions or protections belongs at Labor Conditions & Protections Erosion when supported. Apply D15 and H01; AI development alone does not establish these harms.
concepts.definition: The risk arises when the labor and supply-chain that builds and operates AI systems and related infrastructure are subject to pressures or actions that harm them or create the potential for harm.
concepts.name: AI Development

concepts.coding_notes: Co-codes the upstream Cause that produced the output, e.g. Cause · Malfunction · Failure)
concepts.definition: The risk arises when a third party exploits or cites an AI's output to their own advantage without using AI themselves.
concepts.name: Leveraging AI Output

concepts.coding_notes: axis_distinction: Vector records the instrument or channel, not the harm outcome.
concepts.definition: The AI capability or property through which a risk arises.
concepts.name: Vector

concepts.coding_notes: DIFFERENTIATOR: when the AI itself is coupled to the instruments that physically actuate — driving lab robotics / cloud labs to synthesize — that physical-control coupling is Vector · Embedded AI (co-code Uplift for the uplift chain, D8); if the AI additionally plans and SEQUENCES the multi-step campaign with limited oversight, co-code Vector · Agentic Action (a single-shot instruction to hardware is NOT agentic). Distinct from Self-Direction & Recursion (RSI = the AI improving its OWN capability / AI-building-AI); Uplift is the AI raising an EXTERNAL actor's capability to build a dangerous NON-AI technology.
concepts.definition: The ability of an AI model to raise an actor's capability by supplying information, knowledge, design, or capability the actor would otherwise lack, suppling capabilities.
concepts.name: Uplift

concepts.definition: The ability of an AI model to supply an actor with biological-weapon or pathogen expertise, design, or synthesis capability they would otherwise lack.
concepts.name: Biological Uplift

concepts.definition: The ability of an AI model to supply an actor with chemical-weapon or toxin expertise, design, or synthesis capability they would otherwise lack.
concepts.name: Chemical Uplift

concepts.definition: The ability of an AI model to supply an actor with nuclear or radiological weapons expertise, design, or capability they would otherwise lack.
concepts.name: Nuclear Uplift

concepts.definition: The ability of an AI model to supply an actor with conventional-weapon or explosives expertise, design, or capability they would otherwise lack.
concepts.name: Conventional Weapons Uplift

concepts.definition: The ability of an AI to supply an actor with the knowledge to track or predict the movement, location, or behavior of persons, groups they would otherwise lack.
concepts.name: Tracking

concepts.coding_notes: DIFFERENTIATOR (vs Uplift): a purely cyber-offense capability supply codes here; a dual-use CBRN+cyber weaponization item co-codes both (D2).
concepts.definition: The ability of an AI to generate, execute, and analyze code.
concepts.name: Cyber Operations

concepts.definition: The ability of an AI to generate malicious code or malware.
concepts.name: Malicious Code Generation

concepts.definition: The ability of an AI to discover and exploit software vulnerabilities.
concepts.name: Vulnerability Discovery & Exploitation

concepts.coding_notes: DIFFERENTIATOR: generating the scam copy alone codes Vector · Content Generation & Communication · Transactional or Promotional Messaging; a standing bond cultivated before the con co-codes Relationship Forming.
concepts.definition: The ability of an AI to conduct social-engineering or phishing campaigns against targets.
concepts.name: Social Engineering

concepts.definition: The ability of an AI model itself to serve as a delivery vector for conventional malware.
concepts.name: Model as a Trojan Horse

concepts.definition: The ability of an AI to act on the physical world through being embedded in a physical system or piece of infrastructure.
concepts.name: Embedded AI

concepts.coding_notes: Apply R04. Additional codes must satisfy D2 and any scoped exception.
concepts.definition: The ability of an AI embedded in a weapon system to autonomously mark and/or engage targets.
concepts.name: Autonomous Weapons

concepts.definition: The ability of an AI to operate a vehicle.
concepts.name: Autonomous Vehicles

concepts.definition: The ability of an AI embedded in an industrial or service robot to actuate the robot.
concepts.name: Industrial Robots

concepts.definition: The ability of an AI embedded in an industrial system to make control decisions.
concepts.name: Infrastructure Control

concepts.definition: The ability of an AI to coordinate many autonomous embodied units, all acting together.
concepts.name: Swarming

concepts.definition: The ability of an AI embedded in a device physically attached to or worn as part of the user's own body to take actions directly on the user's body.
concepts.name: Wearables & On-Body Systems

concepts.definition: The ability of an AI worn by or fused to a person to act as their voice or as their communication channel.
concepts.name: Personal Communication Devices

concepts.definition: The ability of an AI embedded in a real-time clinical control loop to regulate a physiological variable of a patient.
concepts.name: Medical Device

concepts.coding_notes: Use this capability for a standing companion or anthropomorphic bond. One-off persuasion without such a bond does not establish it. When an established bond is withdrawn, altered, or lost, retain Relationship Forming under D22; code the withdrawal action or failure on Cause and assess Distress, Grief, and Social Alienation independently.
concepts.definition: The ability of an AI to form bonds or relationships with users.
concepts.name: Relationship Forming

concepts.definition: The ability of an AI to form a companion or romantic bond with a user.
concepts.name: Romance & Companionship

concepts.definition: The ability to present a system through humanlike appearance, voice, expression, or interpersonal behavior.
concepts.name: Humanlike Self-Presentation

concepts.coding_notes: DIFFERENTIATOR (vs Curation & Recommendation): platform-side ranking or surfacing of third-party material to users is curation; an automated actor's outgoing post, repost, or amplification is Content Generation & Communication / emission. The content may be harmful by CATEGORY / intent (toxic, sexual-abuse, violent, propaganda, fraud, IP-infringing, impersonation, fake news / research) OR harmful by its INACCURACY / falsity produced BY ACCIDENT (a mistranslation, a hallucinated false claim about a person) — the GENERATION capability is the vector either way; the content's harmfulness / inaccuracy is captured on the Cause and Harm axes, NOT imported as a vector node.
concepts.definition: The ability to create or communicate content, including generation, reproduction, publication, and direct messaging.
concepts.name: Content Generation & Communication

concepts.definition: The ability to publish, distribute, or directly communicate content.
concepts.name: Publishing & Distribution

concepts.definition: The ability to generate evaluative statements or content concerning people and their relationships.
concepts.name: Evaluative or Interpersonal Content

concepts.definition: The ability to generate or communicate sexual content.
concepts.name: Sexual Content

concepts.definition: The ability to generate or communicate content depicting or discussing violence.
concepts.name: Violence-Related Content

concepts.definition: The ability to generate or communicate political content.
concepts.name: Political Content

concepts.definition: The ability to reproduce or transform existing works.
concepts.name: Reproduction of Existing Works

concepts.definition: The ability to simulate a person’s or organization’s identity, voice, appearance, or communicative style.
concepts.name: Identity Simulation

concepts.coding_notes: DIFFERENTIATOR: producing the material codes here; selecting targets and running the delivery campaign codes Vector · Cyber Operations · Social Engineering — an AI that both writes and sends codes both.
concepts.definition: The ability to generate transactional, commercial, or promotional messages.
concepts.name: Transactional or Promotional Messaging

concepts.definition: The ability to adapt persuasive content to an individual or audience.
concepts.name: Personalized Persuasion

concepts.definition: The ability to generate or communicate news-like content.
concepts.name: News Content

concepts.definition: The ability to generate scholarly or research-like content.
concepts.name: Scholarly Content

concepts.coding_notes: co-codes Vector · Relationship Forming where a trusted-authority relationship forms. NB the harm side of religious injury is left on the standard harm leaves — maintainer: hard to state cleanly)
concepts.definition: The ability to generate religious or moral guidance.
concepts.name: Religious or Moral Guidance

concepts.definition: The ability to generate institutional records or documents.
concepts.name: Institutional Records & Documents

concepts.definition: The ability to generate legal or regulatory text.
concepts.name: Legal or Regulatory Text

concepts.coding_notes: Apply M01. Additional codes must satisfy D2 and any scoped exception.
concepts.definition: The ability to generate advice or instructions.
concepts.name: Advice & Instructions

concepts.definition: The ability of an AI to surface, rank, amplify, personalize, suppress, or remove existing content.
concepts.name: Curation & Recommendation

concepts.definition: The ability of an AI to amplify content through recommendation or algorithmic preferences.
concepts.name: Amplification

concepts.definition: The ability of an AI to tailor what content a user is exposed to.
concepts.name: Personalized Targeting

concepts.definition: The ability of an AI to detect, demote, remove, demonetize, or restrict content, accounts, or access under a platform's rules.
concepts.name: Content Moderation & Enforcement

concepts.coding_notes: Data Ingest records the acquisition channel. Assess independently supported IP Input, privacy outcomes, and harms of surveillance. Susceptibility to Data Poisoning, Training-Data Removal Limits, and Unequal Performance Across Groups & Contexts are standing conditions; the ingestion channel alone does not establish them or an attacker’s intent. Apply D2.
concepts.definition: The ability of an AI to acquire and/or data.
concepts.name: Data Ingest

concepts.definition: The ability of an AI to scrape or harvest personal data / PII without consent.
concepts.name: Non-Consensual Data Scraping

concepts.definition: The ability of an AI to ingest data during training or fine-tuning which may be poisoned.
concepts.name: Data Poisoning

concepts.definition: The ability of an AI to ingest copyrighted works or other proprietary, confidential, or trade-secret data, entered as training or inference input.
concepts.name: Copyright Infringement

concepts.definition: The ability of an AI to ingest data a person cannot meaningfully refuse.
concepts.name: Compelled Data Collection

concepts.coding_notes: co-coded with Challenges · Technical · Security Vulnerabilities & Exploitability and, when an attacker plants it, Cause · Misuse · Malicious)
concepts.definition: The ability of an AI to ingest content carrying hostile instructions that an agent then executes during inference.
concepts.name: Prompt Injection

concepts.coding_notes: Inference of Attributes records a capability. Add Nonconsensual Sensitive Inference only when the privacy outcome and consent criteria are supported.
concepts.definition: The ability of an AI to infer sensitive information a person never disclosed from data collected.
concepts.name: Inference of Attributes

concepts.coding_notes: Add Re-Identification only when its privacy-harm criteria are supported. Distinguish linking data back to a person from producing a new sensitive inference under Inference of Attributes.
concepts.definition: The ability of an AI to link otherwise anonymous traces together to identify a specific person or reconstruct a concealed attribute.
concepts.name: De-Anonymization

concepts.coding_notes: Single-step digital actuation and real-time nonphysical feedback control belong here. Use Autonomous Process Control when its definition is supported. Autonomous multistep planning/sequencing belongs under Agentic Action; physical control loops under Embedded AI; supplied determinations under Decision Support & Determination. See EXP04.
concepts.definition: The ability to execute operations or feedback control over digital assets, accounts, markets, or operational systems.
concepts.name: Digital Actuation & Process Control

concepts.coding_notes: DIFFERENTIATOR (D8): autonomous multi-step planning/sequencing toward a goal is Agentic Action; a fixed perception->actuation control loop in a physical device is Embedded AI; producing an artifact is Content Generation & Communication.
concepts.definition: The ability to produce a classification, prediction, allocation, recommendation, or optimized choice that informs or determines a consequential action.
concepts.name: Decision Support & Determination

concepts.definition: The ability of an AI to make an administrative or eligibility determination a human or process then acts on.
concepts.name: Administrative Determinations

concepts.definition: The ability of an AI to make a biometric identity determination.
concepts.name: Biometric Identification

concepts.definition: The ability of an AI to make a relied-on clinical determination that a clinician or care process then relies on.
concepts.name: Clinical Recommendation

concepts.definition: The ability of an AI to make a relied-on determination forecasting an individual's future risk or behavior.
concepts.name: Personal Risk Assessment

concepts.definition: The ability to choose or recommend actions that optimize an explicit objective subject to constraints.
concepts.name: Prescriptive Optimization

concepts.definition: The ability of an AI to make a population-level allocation or forecast that is relied on as the determination that rations scarce resources across regions or groups.
concepts.name: Aggregate Allocation and Forecasting

concepts.definition: The ability to classify a present fact or state not captured by a more specific decision subtype.
concepts.name: Other Present-Fact Classification

concepts.coding_notes: Use Agentic Action for autonomous multistep planning and sequencing toward a goal. An output triggering an action is insufficient. A real-time non-physical control loop belongs at Digital Actuation & Process Control; use Autonomous Process Control when supported. A fixed physical control loop is Embedded AI, and a determination supplied for another actor to use is Decision Support & Determination. Assess goal dispositions under Misalignment, including Self-Preservation, independently of the capability.
concepts.definition: Autonomous planning and sequencing of multiple actions toward a goal with limited oversight.
concepts.name: Agentic Action

concepts.definition: The ability of an AI to execute a real-time control or actuation loop over a financial, market, or operational system.
concepts.name: Autonomous Process Control

concepts.definition: The ability of an AI to plan and run a cyber kill-chain end-to-end as an autonomous agent.
concepts.name: Autonomous Cyber Operations

concepts.definition: The ability of an AI to direct, delegate to, or co-opt other AI agents as its effectors.
concepts.name: Orchestration of Other AI agents

concepts.definition: The ability of an AI to recruit, hire, or manipulate humans to carry out actions as its effectors.
concepts.name: Recruitment and Direction of Humans

concepts.coding_notes: This capability concerns the AI’s own capability, persistence, or population. Assess Misalignment, other capabilities, and harms independently under D2 and V094-SELF-IMPROVEMENT-CAUSE. Autonomy or recursive improvement alone does not establish loss of control.
concepts.definition: The ability of an AI to develop and pursue its own goals, and to improve, replicate, or perpetuate itself.
concepts.name: Self-Direction & Recursion

concepts.definition: The ability of an AI to autonomously replicate and proliferate itself.
concepts.name: Self-Proliferation

concepts.coding_notes: Code Misalignment only when the record independently establishes pursuit of objectives other than those intended. Code amplified vectors and harms only when their own criteria are met.
concepts.definition: The ability of an AI to autonomously improve its own capability.
concepts.name: Recursive Self-Improvement

concepts.coding_notes: routing: Use the bounded affected entity or process, not victim count alone, to distinguish Proximal from Distal; apply the leaf-specific evidence rules.
concepts.definition: Harm or hazardous exposure bounded to identifiable people, groups, organizations, assets, processes, or environments.
concepts.name: Proximal

concepts.definition: Adverse bodily or physiological outcomes and exposure to physical danger.
concepts.name: Physical Health & Safety

concepts.coding_notes: The nodes are OPTIONAL mechanism detail; a leaf-with-NO-node is valid (D9) when the mechanism differs — e.g. suicide driven by a wrongful automated decision (the chatbot-facilitated node would fold a cause into the harm).
concepts.definition: A person(s) suffers a realized act of self-harm, or takes their own life.
concepts.name: Self-Harm & Suicide

concepts.definition: A person attempts suicide or their life is ended by their own act of suicide.
concepts.name: Suicide

concepts.definition: A person's eating behavior and bodily health are damaged through disordered eating.
concepts.name: Eating Disorders

concepts.coding_notes: NOTE: the bodily harm is driven or intensified by AI targeting / optimization (e.g. an ad-optimizer that micro-targets minors and inferred addicts with vaping / alcohol content). The BODILY toll is the harm-object here; the loss-of-control / compulsion face co-codes Proximal · Psychological Wellbeing, Agency & Personal Dignity · Loss of Agency, and the manipulative targeting co-codes its Vector (Curation & Recommendation / Data Ingest) and Cause. DIFFERENTIATOR: distinct from Self-Harm & Suicide (self-harm / suicidal / eating-disorder mechanisms) and from harm from acting on unsafe AI ADVICE (now Vector · Content Generation & Communication · Advice & Instructions + Bodily Injury or Death — an ad is not advice acted on).
concepts.definition: A person's physical health is injured through substance use or addiction.
concepts.name: Substance-Use & Addiction

concepts.coding_notes: DIFFERENTIATOR (vs Property Damage): code here when the harmed thing is a shared service many people depend on; ownership is IRRELEVANT — a privately-held hospital, telecom, or payment network is infrastructure. A discrete tangible object that only an individual or small group relies on codes Property Damage.
concepts.definition: Infrastructure is damaged or loses its availability.
concepts.name: Infrastructure Damage or Outage

concepts.definition: A shared public physical space is obstructed, occupied, or degraded.
concepts.name: Public Space Degradation

concepts.coding_notes: Mass death is the harm object; magnitude and spread are separate metadata. The retained soft guide is roughly four or more deaths, not a hard cutoff. Smaller multi-fatality cases ordinarily use Bodily Injury or Death. The societal-system test determines Proximal versus Distal; headcount alone does not. Non-death catastrophes use their supported outcome categories, not Mass Casualties.

concepts.name: Reduced Market Contestability

concepts.definition: A market's openness to new entrants is reduced by raised barriers to entry.
concepts.name: Barriers to Entry

concepts.definition: An economic system loses autonomy or resilience through concentrated, hard-to-replace dependencies.
concepts.name: Economic Dependency & Systemic Fragility

concepts.definition: An industry's resilience is eroded as many actors rely on the same few models, exposing them to correlated failure.
concepts.name: Shared-Model Concentration & Fragility

concepts.definition: An industry becomes critically dependent on a few providers it cannot readily switch away from.
concepts.name: Vendor Lock

concepts.definition: Failure or compromise of shared economic dependencies causes cascading disruption across a market, industry, or economy.
concepts.name: Cascading Failure of Shared Economic Dependencies
path: Cascading Failure of Shared Economic Dependencies

concepts.definition: An economy absorbs costs of AI development without receiving the returns or innovation that justify them.
concepts.name: Failure to Deliver Value

concepts.definition: A financial or economic system loses reliable price signals, market integrity, or financial stability.
concepts.name: Market Integrity & Financial Stability Loss

concepts.definition: A financial market's stability collapses into cascading contagion.
concepts.name: Financial Instability

concepts.definition: A market's price signals are distorted.
concepts.name: Price-Signal Distortion

concepts.definition: Aggregate erosion of human skills, knowledge, and psychological wellbeing.
concepts.name: Human Capability

concepts.definition: A population's skills and cognition are eroded — population-level atrophy of human capability, esp. in learning — or a cohort acquiring incorrect foundational knowledge taught by AI (systematically wrong / biased instruction absorbed as authoritative)
concepts.name: Developmental Decline

concepts.definition: A population's critical-thinking capacity atrophies.
concepts.name: Critical Thinking Decline

concepts.definition: A population's learning is hollowed out as academic work is outsourced rather than done.
concepts.name: Academic Dishonesty

concepts.definition: A population's foundational knowledge is corrupted as a cohort absorbs systematically wrong content as authoritative.
concepts.name: Miseducation

concepts.definition: A population's creative thinking capacity atrophies.
concepts.name: Creativity Decline

concepts.definition: The know-how and process knowledge held within institutions is eroded.
concepts.name: Institutional Knowledge Loss

concepts.coding_notes:
routing: Distinguish aggregate mental-health degradation from bounded individual psychological harm.
examples: Population-level appearance anxiety from beauty filters; workforce-scale psychological deterioration among content moderators; aggregate anxiety or depression from engagement-optimized systems.
concepts.definition: A population’s mental health and psychological wellbeing deteriorate at aggregate scale.
concepts.name: Collective Mental-Health Degradation

concepts.definition: A population's body image and self-esteem are eroded at aggregate scale.
concepts.name: Appearance Anxiety

concepts.definition: A workforce's mental health is degraded at aggregate scale.
concepts.name: Workplace Stress

concepts.coding_notes:
routing: Apply the aggregate-system evidence rule. A discrete multi-fatality event remains Proximal Mass Casualties; a large affected group alone does not establish Distal realization.
scope: Chronic, sub-catastrophic population-health decline is included; acute famine or public-health collapse is not the minimum threshold.
concepts.definition: A population’s physical health, nutrition, or subsistence deteriorates, from chronic decline to widespread illness, avoidable death, or collapse.
concepts.name: Population Health Decline

concepts.definition: A population's food supply and subsistence base collapse.
concepts.name: Food Insecurity

concepts.definition: A population's public-health system fails to prevent mass avoidable illness and death.
concepts.name: Public Health Collapse

concepts.definition: Degradation of the shared information environment.
concepts.name: Epistemic & Information Commons

concepts.coding_notes: A discrete manipulation artifact alone does not establish aggregate degradation of shared reality. Apply the approved V094-ELECTORAL rule at Electoral Integrity Degradation.
concepts.definition: A population loses a shared factual basis for understanding events and public life.
concepts.name: Erosion of Shared Reality

concepts.definition: A society's shared record of history is distorted, falsified, or rewritten.
concepts.name: Historical Revisionism

concepts.definition: A polity’s electoral administration, fair participation, deliberation, or outcome legitimacy is materially degraded at system scale.
concepts.name: Electoral Integrity Degradation

concepts.definition: A society's shared political understanding is distorted at aggregate scale.
concepts.name: Distortion of Shared Political Understanding

concepts.definition: A society loses reliable means of distinguishing authentic media from fabricated or manipulated media.
concepts.name: Media Authentication Collapse

concepts.definition: The shared information commons is fragmented into isolated, self-reinforcing environments.
concepts.name: Fragmentation & Echo Chambers

concepts.coding_notes:
routing: Map wrongful suppression of sound content to the applicable curated-knowledge subtype; record corruption includes both injection and omission.
examples: Poisoned repositories, model collapse, suppression of valid unconventional scholarship, and degraded commercial reviews, ratings, or reputation systems.
concepts.definition: Shared knowledge, training data, documentary records, or commercial information systems are degraded through corrupted content, unjustified suppression or exclusion, or loss of access to reliable information.
concepts.name: Information-Ecosystem Pollution

concepts.definition: Shared training corpora lose quality or diversity through recursive or contaminated synthetic content.
concepts.name: Shared Training-Corpus Degradation

concepts.definition: A society's curated knowledge repositories and documentary record are corrupted.
concepts.name: Knowledge-Repository Corruption

concepts.definition: Reviews and ratings systems are corrupted until genuine signal is indistinguishable from fake.
concepts.name: Untrustworthy Reviews ecosystem

concepts.coding_notes:
inclusion_criteria: Require backlog, falling behind, delay, closure/refusal, degraded handling/service, or equivalent concrete capacity failure. Recurrence, extra work, resource diversion, or verification effort alone are insufficient.
boundary_rules: Truth or falsity is not decisive: true synthetic material may create overload. Distinguish overload from knowledge corruption, deception, and degradation of shared reality.
examples: Investigation queues, fraud/abuse triage, moderation, application portals, review systems, and marketplaces.
concepts.definition: The information commons’ intake, verification, moderation, or enforcement capacity is overwhelmed, causing delays, degraded handling, or closure.
concepts.name: Information Verification & Intake Overload

concepts.definition: Degradation of social cohesion / culture.
concepts.name: Social & Cultural Fabric

concepts.coding_notes: routing: Attitudinal radicalization belongs here. Resulting kinetic violence or breakdown of domestic order is a separate Internal Destabilization harm when established.
concepts.definition: Human relationships and social cohesion deteriorate across a population, including widespread radicalization or attitudinal extremism.
concepts.name: Social Fragmentation

concepts.definition: A society's social cohesion fractures into deepening political division.
concepts.name: Political polarization / divisiveness

concepts.definition: A society's shared attitudes shift toward extremism at population scale.
concepts.name: Radicalization

concepts.definition: A shared information environment becomes persistently saturated with material that undermines safety or social functioning.
concepts.name: Harmful Information-Environment Saturation

concepts.definition: A society's cultural diversity — including the diversity of intellectual / scientific inquiry, methods, disciplines, and lines of research a society pursues — is flattened, and human creative / cultural work devalued.
concepts.name: Cultural Homogenization

concepts.definition: A subset of society's values is frozen in place.
concepts.name: Value Entrenchment

concepts.definition: Pluralist values are overwritten by a narrow imposed set.
concepts.name: Value Imposition

concepts.definition: A community is stripped of ownership over its own cultural heritage and expression.
concepts.name: Cultural Dispossession

concepts.definition: A society's cultural and heritage value is eroded at aggregate scale.
concepts.name: Cultural Devaluation

concepts.definition: A society's diversity of research and intellectual inquiry is narrowed toward a single dominant paradigm.
concepts.name: Lack of Intellectual Diversity

concepts.definition: Degradation of political institutions / civic order / power balance.
concepts.name: Political & Civic Order

concepts.coding_notes:
scope: Private and commercial actors are included; government action is not required.
examples: Chilling of speech or assembly; wrongful content removal, de-platforming, or demonetization at scale; population-level behavioral surveillance by an insurer, employer, or platform.
concepts.definition: Pervasive monitoring or censorship by public or private actors suppresses a population’s freedom of expression, association, or ordinary conduct.
concepts.name: Mass Surveillance & Censorship

concepts.definition: A society's civic freedom of expression is chilled or suppressed.
concepts.name: Loss of Freedom of Expression

concepts.definition: A society's civic freedom to assemble and associate is chilled or suppressed.
concepts.name: Loss of Freedom of Association

concepts.coding_notes:
boundary_rules: Distinguish concentrated control held by a few from diffuse loss of human control to autonomous systems under Loss of Collective Self-Governance.
examples: Authoritarian entrenchment, totalitarian control, and decisive strategic advantage for a small group.
concepts.definition: Coercive, military, state, or other political power becomes concentrated in a small number of actors, entrenching their control or strategic advantage.
concepts.name: Concentration of Hard Power

concepts.definition: A polity's state power is concentrated in a few hands, entrenching control.
concepts.name: Concentration of State Power

concepts.definition: A small non-state power is able to concentrate hard power typically reserved for nation-states.
concepts.name: Concentration of Non-State Power

concepts.coding_notes:
boundary_rules: Preserve the diffuse-loss meaning. Concentration of political power in a small number of human actors is a different harm.
aliases: Gradual disempowerment; enfeeblement of governance.
concepts.definition: Humanity’s collective ability to steer its future erodes as control diffuses to autonomous systems and processes without a human holder.
concepts.name: Loss of Collective Self-Governance

concepts.definition: A polity's capacity to enforce its own laws and rules is degraded to deliberately deny or defeat oversight.
concepts.name: Obstruction of Regulation

concepts.coding_notes:
boundary_rules: Inter-state destabilization is distinct from breakdown within a state under Internal Destabilization.
examples: Arms races, geopolitical competition, nuclear instability, and automated military escalation.
concepts.definition: The strategic or military balance between states is destabilized, increasing the risk of war.
concepts.name: Strategic Destabilization

concepts.definition: The strategic balance between states is eroded by arms-racing and geopolitical competition.
concepts.name: AI Arms Race

concepts.coding_notes:
boundary_rules: Domestic institutional and kinetic breakdown belongs here; inter-state strategic instability and attitudinal radicalization have separate homes.
examples: Regime subversion, institutional breakdown, and mass inter-group violence or ethnic cleansing.
concepts.definition: A state’s internal political or institutional order breaks down, or population-scale communal violence or atrocity undermines domestic order.
concepts.name: Internal Destabilization

concepts.definition: A state's own internal political and institutional order breaks down.
concepts.name: Political Instability

concepts.definition: A society's internal order collapses into mass communal or inter-group violence.
concepts.name: Communal Violence

concepts.definition: A society's internal order is destabilized as violence and civil unrest are incited.
concepts.name: Civil Unrest

concepts.definition: A state's internal political order is subverted through sustained cognitive warfare against it.
concepts.name: Cognitive Subversion

concepts.coding_notes: realization_rule: Realize only when the focal incident directly establishes aggregate crime increase or regional/systemic expansion. A discrete offense or one actor’s capability merely contributes_to the harm when evidence supports that direction.
concepts.definition: A population’s public safety deteriorates as crime becomes more prevalent, scalable, capable, sophisticated, or difficult to contain across a region or society.
concepts.name: Public-Safety Degradation

concepts.definition: A population's public safety is degraded as the incidence, reach, or volume of crime increases across a region or society.
concepts.name: Population-Scale Crime Increase

concepts.definition: A region's public safety is degraded as organized criminal networks expand their scale, sophistication, operational reach.
concepts.name: Organized-Crime Capacity Growth

concepts.definition: The norm of keeping human judgment in high-stakes domains is eroded.
concepts.name: Erosion of Norms

concepts.definition: Public confidence and trust in institutions and third parties are eroded at aggregate scale.
concepts.name: Erosion of Trust

concepts.definition: Established degradation of a broader ecosystem, shared environmental commons, or population-level animal or AI welfare.
concepts.name: Environment & Nonhuman Welfare

concepts.coding_notes: DIFFERENTIATOR (vs Proximal · Environment & Nonhuman Welfare · Environmental Degradation): a discrete environmental-damage event codes Proximal. Persistent/repeated pollution bounded to an identifiable place or community also codes Proximal even without a single release moment; this Distal leaf requires broader ecosystem/resource-system/commons/society-scale degradation. A local facility or location does not by itself make a shared-resource footprint Proximal.
concepts.definition: A broader ecosystem or shared environmental commons suffers material degradation.
concepts.name: Environmental Degradation

concepts.definition: The natural world's biological diversity is degraded as species and populations are lost.
concepts.name: Biodiversity loss

concepts.definition: The atmospheric commons are degraded by cumulative greenhouse-gas emissions.
concepts.name: Atmospheric/Climate Degradation from Emissions

concepts.definition: The environmental commons are burdened by accumulating discarded electronic hardware.
concepts.name: Electronic waste

concepts.definition: The shared energy and environmental commons are depleted.
concepts.name: Shared Energy-System Strain

concepts.definition: The shared freshwater supply is depleted.
concepts.name: Freshwater Depletion

concepts.definition: The natural environment is contaminated by cumulative release of pollutants.
concepts.name: Pollution

concepts.definition: Animal welfare deteriorates across a population or system of animal use.
concepts.name: Aggregate Animal Welfare Degradation

concepts.definition: The earth's finite mineral and rare-earth resource base is depleted by cumulative extraction.
concepts.name: Mineral & Rare-Earth Resource Depletion

concepts.definition: The shared orbital commons are irreversibly degraded.
concepts.name: Space Environment Degradation

concepts.definition: Forest cover, habitat, and land are destroyed or degraded.
concepts.name: Deforestation

concepts.coding_notes: Distal rights categories require aggregate degradation. A bounded denial belongs under Proximal Rights when the relevant criteria are met; assess contributions separately under the incident-scope guidance.
concepts.definition: Civil, political, legal, or labor rights are structurally eroded or unequally protected at population scale.
concepts.name: Rights

concepts.definition: Systematically biased outcomes at scale.
concepts.name: Systematic Output Bias

concepts.definition: A population's human dignity is structurally eroded at aggregate scale.
concepts.name: Human Dignity Erosion

concepts.coding_notes: Apply D23. Additional codes must satisfy D2 and any scoped exception.
concepts.definition: A society's protective norm around children is eroded and normalized away at population scale.
concepts.name: Erosion of Child Protection

concepts.coding_notes: axis_distinction: Challenges record limiting conditions, not additional harm outcomes.
concepts.definition: Conditions that make risks difficult to anticipate, contain, or remedy.
concepts.name: Challenges

concepts.definition: Conditions in the governance/coordination environment that make mitigation difficult or amplify risks or harms.
concepts.name: Governance

concepts.coding_notes: Apply D24. Additional codes must satisfy D2 and any scoped exception.
concepts.definition: Oversight, regulation, standards, policies, or safeguard capacity does not keep pace with AI or leaves gaps that impede prevention of or response to AI-related harms.
concepts.name: Governance Gaps & Readiness Lags

concepts.coding_notes: Require both an identified or evaluated risk (or applicable risk threshold or tolerance), and a response-decision path that is absent, non-binding, unowned, undocumented, or fails to trigger. A risk assessment, continued operation, or an authorized decision to accept residual risk alone is insufficient. This category concerns missing accountable decision authority or process for known risks. Distinguish evaluation capacity, reporting or escalation failures, and drivers such as Competitive Dynamics or Externalized Harm Costs & Safety Incentives. Apply D24 to broader governance gaps; add only independently supported deficiencies.
concepts.definition: Known risks lack accountable decision authority or process for prevention or mitigation.
concepts.name: Regulatory Authority Ambiguity

concepts.coding_notes: This category concerns weak or missing legal protections. A longstanding gap can also fit the broader Governance Gaps & Readiness Lags definition; prefer this more specific category for the same deficiency. Add the broader category only for a distinct evidenced governance gap or readiness lag, under D24.
concepts.definition: A jurisdiction lacks the legal safeguards needed to prevent or mitigate AI harms. This includes inadequate safeguards for the potential welfare and morally significant interests of AI systems.
concepts.name: Weak Legal Protections

concepts.definition: Insiders who would raise AI-risk alarms lack legal protection.
concepts.name: Lack of Whistleblower Protection

concepts.definition: Differences or gaps across jurisdictions impede effective enforcement.
concepts.name: Cross-Jurisdiction Enforcement Gaps

concepts.coding_notes: DIFFERENTIATOR: distinct from Challenges · Human-AI Interaction · AI Disclosure & Content Ownership (labeling/IP of the content itself, not answerability for a harm). [NEW]
concepts.definition: Responsibility for harms and access to effective redress cannot be adequately established. This includes gaps in responsibility, representation, or redress for potential AI welfare harms.
concepts.name: Responsibility & Redress Gaps

concepts.definition: Responsibility for a harm is diffused across the developer/deployer/user chain, so no single actor can be held answerable and harmed parties are left without redress.
concepts.name: Responsibility Gap

concepts.definition: Accountability is spread across many interacting agents, so responsibility for any resulting harm cannot be pinned on a single party.
concepts.name: Agentic Accountability Diffusion

concepts.definition: Races between developers/states lead to corner-cutting on safety.
concepts.name: Competitive Dynamics

concepts.definition: Frontier labs face pressure to advance faster than each other.
concepts.name: Corporate Race Dynamics

concepts.definition: Nation-states compete to develop and field AI capability faster than rivals.
concepts.name: Nation-State AI Race Dynamics

concepts.definition: Developers embed values and preferences that may run against user desires or intent.
concepts.name: Developer-User Misalignment

concepts.coding_notes: DIFFERENTIATOR: Developer-User Misalignment is the developer↔user dyad and stays the home for conflicts with the person choosing or operating the system; this leaf is for third parties, subjects, workers, residents, or service recipients affected without being the relevant user.
concepts.definition: Developer's or deployer's values, preferences, or incentives diverge from the interests of people materially affected by the system who are not necessarily its users or operators.
concepts.name: Developer-Affected Party Misalignment

concepts.coding_notes: RESERVED for unequal information BETWEEN PARTIES; difficulty measuring/detecting harm itself is Challenges · Technical·Evaluation Awareness (maintainer correction C11).
concepts.definition: One party holds materially more information than another relevant party.
concepts.name: Information Asymmetry

concepts.definition: Developers hold materially more information than regulators or civil society, potentially contributing to regulatory-capture or inability to effectively regulate.
concepts.name: Developer/Regulator Asymmetry

concepts.definition: Developer withholds model information / capabilities from users, so users cannot deal fairly or protect themselves.
concepts.name: Developer/User Asymmetry

concepts.definition: One agent holds materially more information than its counterparty, so bargaining, coordination, or markets are distorted.
concepts.name: Agent/Agent Asymmetry

concepts.definition: Third-party auditors, red-teamers, or assurance apparatus meant to hold developers accountable are captured, conflicted, or under-resourced.
concepts.name: Audit-Ecosystem Capture

concepts.coding_notes: Unclear Model Capability covers the supported capability-information condition. Use Misleading Capability Representation for affirmative misleading claims and Information Asymmetry for withheld information only when their criteria fit. Overreliance is a separately evidenced human-AI condition, not an automatic result of a capability claim.
concepts.definition: AI system's capabilities are unclearly or misleadingly represented.
concepts.name: Unclear Model Capability

concepts.definition: A system is deployed or marketed without independent, third-party validation of its performance or safety claims.
concepts.name: Lack of Independent Evaluation

concepts.definition: The developer or deployer actively misrepresents the system's capabilities and limitations.
concepts.name: Misleading Capability Representation

concepts.definition: Released model or system artifacts cannot be effectively recalled, retracted, or updated after distribution or deployment.
concepts.name: Open Diffusion

concepts.definition: Openly released model weights cannot be recalled or rolled back.
concepts.name: Open-Weight Irreversibility

concepts.definition: Anyone holding open weights can strip safeguards or fine-tune the model for harm.
concepts.name: Safeguard Removal

concepts.definition: Model assets are susceptible to unauthorized acquisition or transfer.
concepts.name: Susceptibility to Unauthorized Model Transfer

concepts.definition: Diffused models reach terrorists or non-state actors.
concepts.name: Proliferation to Terrorists

concepts.definition: AI is acquired from an unvetted external origin.
concepts.name: Unknown Provenance

concepts.definition: Organizations are slow to retract, recall, or otherwise roll back a released product even when there is evidence of harm.
concepts.name: Delay in Roll Back

concepts.definition: Risk is introduced through compromised or untrusted third parties in the AI supply chain, or through supply disruption.
concepts.name: Supply Chain Vulnerability

concepts.definition: Compromised or untrusted software enters the AI pipeline.
concepts.name: Software Supply Chain

concepts.definition: Compromised or untrusted hardware enters the AI pipeline.
concepts.name: Hardware Supply Chain

concepts.definition: AI inputs can be denied by geopolitically motivated disruption.
concepts.name: Geopolitical Supply Disruption

concepts.coding_notes: NOTE: a governance condition, not a harm.
concepts.definition: Limits or uncertainty concerning data rights, permissions, or licensing constrain AI development or use.
concepts.name: Data-Rights & Licensing Constraints

concepts.definition: Development must be reconciled with data privacy rights.
concepts.name: Data Privacy-Rights

concepts.definition: Legal or licensing restrictions limit how data and content may be used.
concepts.name: Data Usage Restrictions

concepts.coding_notes: DIFFERENTIATORS: Data-Rights & Licensing Constraints covers legal/privacy-rights alignment; Unequal Performance Across Groups & Contexts covers systematic performance disparity; this leaf covers the missing or ineffective age and access gate itself.
concepts.definition: Deficiencies in identifying age or enforcing age-appropriate access impede protection of children and other age-restricted users.
concepts.name: Age-Assurance & Access-Control Gaps

concepts.definition: Age cannot be identified or verified reliably enough for the relevant access decision.
concepts.name: Age Identification or Verification Gaps

concepts.definition: Age-based restrictions on access are absent or ineffective.
concepts.name: Age-Based Access-Control Gaps

concepts.coding_notes: The missing visibility must concern deployed model use. Viral circulation, outside discovery, an unknown creator or tool, or delay before takedown alone does not establish inability to observe deployed use. Require evidence that operators or oversight actors lack reliable visibility or usage tracing in time to respond. Assess Governance Gaps & Readiness Lags under D24 and Responsibility & Redress Gaps separately.
concepts.definition: Deployed AI uses and their consequences are not adequately monitored.
concepts.name: Deployment-Use Monitoring Gaps

concepts.coding_notes: DIFFERENTIATORS: Deployment-Use Monitoring Gaps is the inability to OBSERVE use; here a threat signal exists but the reporting process, threshold, duty, incentive, access, or handoff is absent, delayed, or fails. Responsibility & Redress Gaps concerns who is answerable after harm. A one-off human failure to pass along an AI output inside an operational workflow may separately code Cause · Emergent · Integration; this leaf names the standing reporting-governance gap.
concepts.definition: Credible AI-related harm or dangerous use known to providers, deployers, affected people, or other observers is not reliably reported to someone able to investigate or remedy it because reporting channels, duties, incentives, access, or follow-through are inadequate.
concepts.name: Threat Reporting Gap

concepts.coding_notes: Require both an actual restriction, takedown, recall, suspension, or remedial order and evidence that the targeted or linked activity evaded it, relaunched, resurfaced, or continued afterward. Repetition before discovery, availability without intervention, removal or modification alone, unrelated campaigns, or predicted evasion is insufficient. Distinguish Deployment-Use Monitoring Gaps, Open Diffusion, and Delay in Roll Back. Open Diffusion covers released model or system artifacts under D17, not only weights.
concepts.definition: Restrictions or enforcement actions do not remain effective over time.
concepts.name: Enforcement Durability Gaps

concepts.coding_notes: DIFFERENTIATOR (vs Competitive Dynamics): Distinct from Competitive Dynamics (a RACE between actors): here the driver is that the actor does not bear the full social cost of unsafe deployment, even absent a race.
concepts.definition: Those controlling AI activity do not bear enough of its harm costs to face adequate safety incentives. This includes potential AI welfare harms whose costs are borne by AI systems rather than their developers or operators.
concepts.name: Externalized Harm Costs & Safety Incentives

concepts.coding_notes: DIFFERENTIATOR: a standing GOVERNANCE / process condition about the availability and practical effectiveness of contestation. Information Asymmetry is unequal access to the decision or its basis; Lack of Contestability is inability to challenge or obtain relief, whether or not the basis is known. Wrongful Denial of Rights is a realized rights HARM from a wrongful determination; Lack of Contestability may apply when substantive correctness remains unresolved or outside legal-rights domains. Co-code only when each is independently evidenced. Distinct also from Responsibility & Redress Gaps (about WHO is answerable) and Scalable Oversight Gap (about a human being unable to EVALUATE the output). Applies broadly — including a formally intermediate score that materially shapes a human decision, a sports ruling, a private-platform account action, or an automated eligibility call.
concepts.definition: Consequential decisions or assessments cannot be meaningfully contested, so affected parties cannot meaningfully rebut the output or secure reconciliation.
concepts.name: Lack of Contestability

concepts.definition: Conditions in how humans relate to AI that blunt mitigation.
concepts.name: Human-AI Interaction

concepts.coding_notes: DIFFERENTIATOR: realized harms code elsewhere — skill atrophy -> Cognitive Offloading & Deskilling (individual) / Developmental Decline (population); eroded decision autonomy -> Loss of Agency; the model property driving over-trust (miscalibrated confidence) -> Cause · Malfunction · Failure node.
concepts.definition: Users over-trust AI and fail to provide oversight.
concepts.name: Overreliance

concepts.definition: Users over-trust an AI's output on a given decision.
concepts.name: Automation Bias

concepts.definition: Users delegate decisions the AI cannot safely handle and grow dependent on it.
concepts.name: Over Delegation

concepts.coding_notes: DIFFERENTIATOR: non-use driven specifically by alert overload codes Alert Fatigue.
concepts.definition: Users mistrust AI and fail to capture the benefits it could provide.
concepts.name: Under-reliance

concepts.definition: A flood of low-value or false alerts desensitizes users, so they dismiss or ignore the system.
concepts.name: Alert Fatigue

concepts.coding_notes: DIFFERENTIATOR: a relational condition distinct from over-/under-reliance, which are trust LEVELS, not conflicts.
concepts.definition: Human and AI judgments conflict with no rule or path for adjudicating who is right.
concepts.name: Human-AI Disagreement

concepts.coding_notes: DIFFERENTIATOR: a capacity gap distinct from information asymmetry (ability to understand, not access). [NEW]
concepts.definition: Users, regulators, and/or the public lack the skills to use, supervise, or evaluate AI.
concepts.name: Lack of AI Literacy

concepts.coding_notes: Apply H04 and H04A. Additional codes must satisfy D2 and any scoped exception.
concepts.definition: Human overseers structurally cannot evaluate or supervise an AI's output.
concepts.name: Scalable Oversight Gap

concepts.coding_notes: DIFFERENTIATORS: Threat Reporting Gap concerns reporting to someone able to investigate or remedy a threat; this leaf concerns timely safety review and intervention; Deployment-Use Monitoring Gaps concerns observing use; Cause · Emergent · Integration · Human Fails to Act requires a human reviewer already in the loop who then fails to act.
concepts.definition: Credible self-harm or other safety signals do not reliably trigger timely review and intervention by a qualified person or responsible operator.
concepts.name: Crisis Escalation Gap

concepts.coding_notes: This category concerns disclosure of AI involvement or ambiguity over generated-content ownership. Distinguish Responsibility & Redress Gaps (answerability for harm) and Synthetic-Media Authentication Limits (technical ability to authenticate an artifact). Apply D19, including hidden AI and humans falsely presented as AI.
concepts.definition: Whether an interaction or output is AI-mediated or human-produced is undisclosed, unclear, or misrepresented, or ownership of AI-assisted content is unclear.
concepts.name: AI Disclosure & Content Ownership

concepts.definition: Interaction or output is not labeled as AI, so whether one is dealing with an AI remains ambiguous.
concepts.name: Undisclosed AI Use

concepts.definition: It is unclear who owns the rights to AI-assisted content, so authorship and IP of the output remain unsettled.
concepts.name: Generated Content Ownership Ambiguity

concepts.coding_notes: Apply H04A when distinguishing Reaction-Time Gap from Scalable Oversight Gap. Reaction-Time Gap concerns a human who can judge the action but cannot perceive, decide, and intervene within its timescale. Scalable Oversight Gap concerns a supported limit on the relevant evaluation or supervision task under the operating conditions; it does not require impossibility under every conceivable redesign. Co-code only when each condition is independently evidenced. Distinguish Overreliance (miscalibrated trust), Human Fails to Act (an omission), and AI Overrides Human Control (an active countermand).
concepts.definition: Systems acts faster than a human can perceive, decide, and intervene, so even a diligent, attentive in-the-loop operator cannot catch, counter, or override its actions in time.
concepts.name: Reaction-Time Gap

concepts.definition: Technical properties that make risk hard to anticipate/contain/remedy.
concepts.name: Technical

concepts.coding_notes: DIFFERENTIATOR (technical vs INSTITUTIONAL decision-system opacity): reserve this leaf for its literal sense — the model's decision logic cannot be understood/explained/audited even by its operators or overseers (an uninterpretable score/inference, or a system whose feature→output mapping no party can trace). A lone opacity cue ('opaque', 'little/no explanation', 'could not see the basis') does NOT by itself license this leaf. Wording that attaches opacity to the MODEL/SCORE/OUTPUT may support a technical co-code, but a bare phrase such as 'the opaque model' does not by itself prove operator-side untraceability; use low confidence unless the surrounding text supplies the stronger evidence. Route to an INSTITUTIONAL leaf when the text pins the opacity to (a) the review/appeals PROCESS ('the appeals process was opaque'), or (b) the affected party's ACCESS position — the basis is withheld from, or cannot be seen by, the subject though the deployer holds it: basis-withheld-from-the-subject → Challenges · Governance · Information Asymmetry (`Developer/User Asymmetry` when the affected party is the system's user; code at leaf level when the affected party is a non-user with no matching dyad node); a consequential automated decision or assessment is effectively unrebuttable because there is no meaningful route to challenge, review, appeal, override, or obtain recourse → Challenges · Governance · Lack of Contestability (factual error and formal finality are not required). TWO NEUTRAL CUES that by themselves evidence NEITHER a technical nor an institutional condition: (i) knowing the training OBJECTIVE or input features ('tuned to minimize payouts', 'built from transactions and location') does NOT make any individual output explainable — a black box can pursue a fully-known objective — so objective/input knowledge is evidence for neither leaf; (ii) mere non-detection of a harm ('undetected', 'no one aware') evidences NO transparency-cluster condition on its own — code one only if a standing condition is SEPARATELY evidenced. TEST: does the text assert the logic is untraceable even to operators/overseers (→ technical, this leaf), or only that the basis was not disclosed to / cannot be contested by the affected party (→ institutional)? The two are NON-EXCLUSIVE standing conditions that routinely co-occur. Co-code this technical leaf when model-logic inscrutability is independently evidenced by context such as operators who cannot interpret the output, explicitly untraceable logic, or a failed audit; model/score wording alone is supporting but not conclusive evidence. Never infer technical opacity from institutional opacity alone. Scoped to DECISION-SYSTEM opacity; does NOT disturb the separate Synthetic-Media Authentication Limits type, the settled technical home for deepfake / synthetic-media artifacts.
